title: The Apex Peak
blurb: Minutes of a meeting that ended the way its chairman wanted. One director stayed behind.
body: The board meets at night because the chairman prefers it. From the head of the table, share is a thing you discuss after you have already lost. Voss calls the basement a ward. Lang wants a date he can carry to Zurich. Hale says a secret lab is only a number, and numbers die in public.
Pierce Hawkes answers that compliance does not set the ceiling. He does. The minutes record the motion as tabled. They do not record who stayed in the room.
At the window afterward he repeats the pitch to the city until it sounds rotten. A terminal in the next room starts an alarm that was never on the agenda.

title: B3
blurb: The clearance badge still works. Nobody revoked it, because nobody thought he would use it.
body: The cab does not stop at the lobby. Below it is restricted glass, chemical stores, and a floor the company keeps off its own floor plans. Patients to one director. A pipeline to the man who owns the ceiling.
The badge Pierce carries opens every door on Sector 4. That was a courtesy once. Tonight it is how he walks into the one room he signed the budget for and never visited.
He can still think afterward. He is the first to say that is not the same as still being him.

title: The Return
kicker: A call that goes unanswered well
blurb: The halls are too bright. Hale is already on the phone to the other investors.
body: He walks back through the basement without the flashlight. The lamps are the same lamps. They are too bright now, and he says so out loud, twice, as if someone might agree.

Hale rings in the pipe hall. She is furious that he walked out of a board meeting. She wants it rescheduled. He says he can't. She says she will speak with the other investors, and she does not say it kindly.
The cab climbs fifty-eight floors. By the time the doors open he has decided he needs a mirror.

title: The Desk
blurb: The papers are where he left them. He is no longer sure the man who left them is the one standing here.
body: The hall bathroom has the only honest glass on the floor. He looks until the sentence forms: nobody will accept him looking like this. People decide what you are before you speak.
The desk is as he left it. The quarter, the valuation, the clutter of a man who intended to come back. He shoves the papers to the floor and does not wait to watch them land.
He is not staying to be stared at. He is going home.

title: Going Home
blurb: The street has heard about the tower. It has not heard about him. It will.
body: The lobby is a short scene and an ugly one. The receptionist screams and calls the police. Pierce says he is not going back up, and takes the door that opens onto the avenue.

Hawkes Street runs east in wet light. People cross it rather than pass him. Voss texts that the police are on their way to the tower. Whatever he has become, the city is about to learn to be afraid of it in the order he teaches it.
The stairs to the subway are at the end of the block.

title: The Station
blurb: A man on the platform looks a lot like him. The doors of the uptown train are open.
body: The platform smells like rain on iron. A commuter waits by the west car. Beside him stands a darker copy of the same man, and a moment later it is gone.

Another figure steps off the train and talks to the commuter about uptown, this car, saving a seat. It has Pierce's coat and Pierce's walk and a face that has not changed. Pierce asks the one question that matters: how is he talking to him if he is standing here?
Hale calls to say the board went well. The door is still open. It is the only way forward.

title: The Train
blurb: Somebody is always one car ahead. He gets off before Pierce can reach him.
body: The old body rides the uptown 6 with its hand on the pole, as if the train were a room it owned. Pierce follows it through the cars. Each end door opens on different riders and the same back.
Nobody names it. Nobody says why there are two of him. The leak from the basement preferred a man, and it found one.

At a stop with no name the old body gets off. It does not look back. Hale calls to say nothing from B3 reached the street. The doors close in front of him. He gets the street. Somebody else gets the train.

title: The Morning
blurb: The lock still knows his hand. Morning comes anyway, and the news has a name for him.
body: Three blocks. He can walk three blocks. The door of his apartment opens for a hand that is not quite the one it was cut for.

He sleeps, which he does not do. He wakes to a television that has already decided what happened in Hawkes Tower. The anchors name the tower and the chairman. They do not name what is underneath it. They do not need to.
Voss rings, one way. Pierce listens. Somebody is going to have to tell them which one of us walks in.
